**Strategy Brief: Send Minimum Viable Force**
This update refines the agent's attacking logic by calculating the exact `future_garrison + 1` ships required to capture a target. Instead of sending a fixed fraction of available ships, this minimizes over-committing forces to a single target. By conserving ships, the agent can distribute its fleet more efficiently across multiple objectives.

history.hypothesis: Tracking incoming friendly fleets to a target reduces redundant ship dispatches and allows multiple planets to coordinate.
Implementing specialized interception logic for comet planets provides a late-game production advantage.
Calculating tangent vectors to avoid the sun instead of aborting the attack opens up previously blocked tactical trajectories.
Since speed scales logarithmically with fleet size, grouping small dispatches into a single larger fleet improves ETA and interception success.
Squaring the production rate in the target scoring formula prioritizes high-yield planets, compounding late-game advantages.

# Production-Weighted Scoring
This module implements the Production-Weighted Scoring strategy for targeting planets. 
By squaring the production rate in the score formula, it heavily prioritizes high-yield planets.
This approach compounds late-game advantages by ensuring we capture the most valuable resources.

history.hypothesis: Applying a massive multiplier to neutral planets in the early game accelerates the economic snowball effect before enemy engagement.
Replacing the linear 1/dt distance penalty with an exponential decay function prevents fleets from over-committing to distant targets where orbital mechanics make intercepts unpredictable.
